subject: AE
title: Electrical Circuits and Instrumentation
description: Charge, current, and voltage. Voltage and current sources, resistors, capacitors, and inductors. Ohm's Law, Kirchhoff’s Laws, nodal analysis, instrumentation amplifier circuits, impedance. Basics of electrical transducers and data acquisition.

subject: BIOL
title: Advanced Topics in Biology
description: Selected advanced topics in biology. Content varies depending on instructor. May include seminars, independent projects, or specialized themes.
prerequisites: Level at least 4A Biology or instructor consent

subject: CIVE
title: Digital Computation
description: Introduction to digital computation for civil engineers, including programming fundamentals and applications to engineering problems.

subject: CIVE
title: Foundation Engineering
description: Analysis and design of shallow and deep foundations. Topics include bearing capacity, settlement, retaining structures, and slope stability.

subject: EARTH
title: Geochemistry
description: Principles of geochemistry with applications to Earth materials and processes. Topics include isotopes, aqueous chemistry, and thermodynamics in geologic systems.

subject: EARTH
title: Mineralogy
description: Crystal chemistry, symmetry, and classification of minerals. Identification methods and applications to geology and materials science.

subject: EARTH
title: Advanced Hydrogeology
description: Advanced study of groundwater flow and contaminant transport. Topics include modeling, aquifer testing, and groundwater-surface water interactions.

subject: ENVE
title: Digital Computation
description: Introduction to digital computation for environmental engineers. Topics include programming fundamentals, logic, loops, arrays, and engineering applications.

subject: ENVE
title: Environmental Chemistry
description: Chemical principles applied to natural and engineered environmental systems. Topics include equilibria, acid-base, redox, and kinetics in water and soil.

subject: ENVS
title: Field Ecology
description: Introduction to ecological principles through fieldwork. Emphasis on population, community, and ecosystem ecology.

subject: ERS
title: Environmental Assessment
description: Principles and practice of environmental impact assessment. Topics include legislation, project evaluation, mitigation, and monitoring.

subject: GEOE
title: Digital Computation
description: Introduction to digital computation for geological engineers. Programming fundamentals and problem solving for engineering geology applications.

subject: HRM
title: Basic Human Resources Management
description: Introduction to the field of human resources management. Topics include staffing, compensation, labour relations, and employment law.

subject: KIN
title: Introduction to Biomechanics Lab
description: Laboratory exercises in biomechanics. Emphasis on motion analysis, force measurement, and muscle mechanics.

subject: KIN
title: Advanced Biomechanics
description: Advanced study of biomechanics of human movement. Topics include musculoskeletal modeling, joint mechanics, and applications to ergonomics and sport.

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering
description: Overview of mechanical engineering profession. Introduction to engineering design, problem solving, and communication skills.

subject: ME
title: Mechanics of Deformable Solids
description: Stress, strain, torsion, bending, shear, deflection, and combined loading of structural elements.

subject: ME
title: Finite Element Analysis
description: Introduction to finite element methods for structural and thermal analysis. Applications in mechanical and mechatronics engineering.

subject: ME
title: Mechatronics System Design
description: Design methodology for integrated mechanical, electrical, and software systems. Topics include modeling, simulation, control, and prototyping.

subject: MTE
title: Statics
description: Fundamentals of statics for engineers. Force vectors, equilibrium of particles and rigid bodies, trusses, frames, and distributed loads.

subject: PHYS
title: Electricity and Magnetism
description: Electrostatics, magnetostatics, electric circuits, electromagnetic induction, Maxwell's equations, and applications.
